title: Pneumatology and Spiritual Gifts
description: A ministry-focused study of the Holy Spirit and spiritual gifts. Students trace the Spirit's work through the Old Testament, the ministry of Jesus, Pentecost and the early church; study the gifts listed in Romans 12, 1 Corinthians 12-14, Ephesians 4 and 1 Peter 4; compare continuationist, cessationist and 'open but cautious' positions and Pentecostal, charismatic, Wesleyan, Reformed, Catholic and Orthodox perspectives; and develop principles for discerning and pastorally stewarding the gifts in congregational life.

quiz_bank.question: State the strongest cessationist case.
quiz_bank.answer_key: The apostles and prophets were the church's unrepeatable foundation (Eph 2:20); miraculous gifts authenticated them and new revelation (Heb 2:3-4; 2 Cor 12:12); with the canon complete, revelatory gifts ceased; many Fathers observed their decline; modern claims often fail biblical standards.

quiz_bank.question: State the strongest continuationist case.
quiz_bank.answer_key: The NT never teaches cessation; gifts are given until the perfect comes at Christ's return (1 Cor 13:8-12); Pentecost's promise extends to 'all flesh' and future generations (Acts 2:17, 39); Paul commands 'do not forbid tongues' and 'earnestly desire to prophesy'; testimony of gifts continues through church history (Irenaeus, Augustine's later writings).
